bib.title: Recipes for Building an Open-Domain Chatbot
bib.venue: EACL 2021 (Proceedings of the 16th Conference of the European Chapter of the ACL, pages 300-325)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; conversation screenshots (Figs 1, 6, A.16-A.18, A.20, A.22) are images and did not extract

question: Which ingredients (scale, fine-tuning data, decoding) combine to give the best human-rated open-domain chatbot?
hypothesis: Large models fine-tuned on skill-focused data (BST) with tuned decoding (minimum length, beam search) can beat prior chatbots on engagingness and humanness.
contributions: Recipes for 90M, 2.7B and 9.4B parameter chatbots, with models and code released
Evidence that BST fine-tuning and minimum-length constrained beam search matter more than perplexity
Failure-case analysis, with inconclusive unlikelihood and retrieve-and-refine experiments

method.summary: Pre-train Seq2Seq Transformers (90M, 2.7B, 9.4B) on filtered pushshift.io Reddit, fine-tune on ConvAI2, Empathetic Dialogues, Wizard of Wikipedia and Blended Skill Talk, and compare decoding settings with ACUTE-Eval. Also test poly-encoder retrieval, retrieve-and-refine (dialogue and Wikipedia knowledge) and unlikelihood training.

datasets.name: pushshift.io Reddit
datasets.size: 1.50B comments; 56.8B label BPE tokens; 88.8B context tokens
datasets.split: 4096 chunks stratified by thread ID; last two reserved for validation and test, each about 0.02% (~360k comments)
datasets.source: Pushshift Reddit dump through July 2019 (Baumgartner et al. 2020)
datasets.preprocessing: Remove comment and children if bot author, non-English subreddit, removed/deleted, >2048 chars without spaces, >128 BPE tokens, <5 characters, contains URL, starts non-ASCII, depth >7; context and response truncated to 128 BPE tokens

datasets.name: Meena human-bot logs and human-human employee logs
datasets.split: public logs, some toxic conversations removed

models.name: Poly-encoder retriever 256M
models.init_from: Humeau et al. 2019 / Smith et al. 2020

models.name: Poly-encoder retriever 622M
models.init_from: MLM pre-training on same data and dictionary as large generative models

training.objective: MLE; poly-encoder cross-entropy ranking with in-batch negatives; optional unlikelihood (L_MLE + alpha L_UL, alpha 0.25); alpha-blending (replace retrieved reply with gold alpha% of time, alpha 0.5 for RetNRef)
training.lr: 2e-4 max (2.7B pre-train); 1.15e-4 max (9.4B pre-train); 1e-6 to 1e-5 max (fine-tune)
training.batch_size: about 500k label BPE tokens (2.7B and 9.4B); 512 elements for retriever
training.steps: about 200k SGD updates (2.7B, not converged; 9.4B, not overfitting); fine-tuned to convergence
training.precision: mixed precision, FP32 gradients and optimizer state, FP16 parameters, dynamic loss scaling

other.parallelism: Megatron-LM style model parallelism in pre-training; GPipe-style in fine-tuning

inference.decoding: Chosen: beam search, beam size 10, minimum length 20 BPE tokens, 3-gram blocking over context and response. Compared: beam 1/30, top-k (k=40), sample-and-rank (20 samples), predictive length (4-class classifier).
inference.samples: 100 human-bot conversations per model; about 140 self-chat trials per pair
inference.prompting: Persona (two sentences) in context; WoW topic name one third of the time; conversations start with 'Hi!'
inference.retrieval: Dialogue retrieval: poly-encoder reply appended to generator input with separator. Knowledge retrieval: TF-IDF inverted index over Wikipedia dump, transformer ranker picks one sentence; classifier decides whether to retrieve per turn

metrics.name: ACUTE-Eval engagingness
metrics.definition: Pairwise judgement of complete dialogues, 'Who would you prefer to talk to for a long conversation?'

metrics.name: Hits@1/K
metrics.definition: recall@1 ranking the gold label among K-1 random candidates

baselines: human-human logs (employees; crowdworkers in BST paper)
eval.protocol: Crowdworker human-bot chats (100 per model, min 14 turns); two-tailed binomial test, p<0.05 or p<0.01; self-chat ACUTE-Eval for hyperparameter selection

availability.code: released (ParlAI fine-tuning and evaluation code), URL not stated in text
availability.data: conversation logs with crowdworkers released with the code

results.claim: Best model (BST Generative 2.7B) beats Meena 75% to 25% on engagingness.
results.setup: Human-bot ACUTE-Eval vs publicly released Meena logs; two-tailed binomial test p<0.01
results.quote: the latter in a pairwise comparison 75% to 25% in terms of engagingness, and by 65% to 35% in terms of humanness (both statistically signiﬁcant, two-tailed binomial test, p < 0.01)

results.claim: Best model beats Meena 65% to 35% on humanness.
results.quote: by 65% to 35% in terms of humanness

results.claim: Plain BST Generative 2.7B scores 49% against human-human employee logs (not significant).
results.metric: engagingness win rate vs human logs
results.setup: Human-bot ACUTE-Eval engagingness vs Adiwardana et al. employee logs; 100 conversations
results.quote: e.g. 49% to 51% for our 2.7B generative model compared to human-human logs

results.claim: Adding Wikipedia knowledge retrieval (Wiz Generative 2.7B) gave 47% vs 49% for the same-size model without it; authors say reading knowledge only had a negative impact.
results.metric: engagingness win rate vs human logs
results.setup: Human-bot ACUTE-Eval, engagingness question, 100 crowdworker conversations of at least 14 turns per model (starting 'Hi!'), compared against employee human-human logs from Adiwardana et al. 2020; win % of the model
results.quote: Unfortunately the reading of knowledge only had a negative impact in ACUTE-Evals compared to a similarly sized model without knowledge retrieval (Figure 2).

results.claim: RetNRef (dialogue retrieval, 622M/2.7B) scores 46% vs 49% for the plain generator; no improvement once generator decoding is tuned.
results.metric: engagingness win rate vs human logs
results.setup: Human-bot ACUTE-Eval, engagingness question, 100 crowdworker conversations of at least 14 turns per model (starting 'Hi!'), compared against employee human-human logs from Adiwardana et al. 2020; win % of the model
results.quote: We ﬁnd RetNRef models (both dialogue version and using knowledge retrieval) do not improve over their generative counterparts when using the best decoding schemes for the generative models

results.claim: Without the 20-token minimum length (standard beam) the 2.7B model falls to 21% vs human logs (significant).
results.metric: engagingness win rate vs human logs
results.setup: Human-bot ACUTE-Eval, engagingness question, 100 crowdworker conversations of at least 14 turns per model (starting 'Hi!'), compared against employee human-human logs from Adiwardana et al. 2020; win % of the model
results.table: Fig 2, row BST Generative (2.7B) std. beam, win column (21 **)
results.note: Fig 2 is a figure whose text extracted; the 21 occurs in extracted text

results.claim: Minimum beam length 20 beats unconstrained beam 83% to 17% in self-chat; predictive length gives 81% to 19%.
results.setup: Self-chat ACUTE-Eval engagingness, about 140 trials per pair, Generative 2.7B BST, min length 20 BPE tokens
results.quote: show that both methods improve signiﬁcantly over not controlling the length (83% to 17%; 81% to 19%)

results.claim: Average response length is about 21 tokens with the minimum-length constraint vs 9.5 without; Meena 10.4, humans 18.0.
results.quote: is around 21 tokens, vs. 9.5 to-kens without

results.claim: Beam size 10 is a sweet spot; beam 30 is on par with sampling (48% to 52%), none significant.
results.setup: Self-chat ACUTE-Eval; top-k k=40, sample-and-rank 20 samples
results.quote: which is then on par with sampling methods (48% to 52%), although none of these results is signiﬁcant
results.note: Text hyphenation 'signiﬁ-cant' in PDF; quote normalized

results.claim: Fine-tuning on BST tasks beats pre-training only 60% to 40% in self-chat.
results.quote: Fine-tuning on the smaller, more focused BST datasets leads to signiﬁcant improvements (60% to 40%)

results.claim: The 9.4B model scores below the 2.7B in engagingness despite lower perplexity; head-to-head 56% win for the 2.7B.
results.quote: which resulted in a 56% win for the smaller model

results.claim: BST fine-tuning cuts average BST-validation perplexity 2.7B from 12.0 to 9.0 (9.4B: 11.2 to 8.6); RetNRef 2.7B 9.8.
results.table: Table 3, rows 2.7B and 9.4B, columns Pre-train only and BST Gen
results.note: Table 5 prints 8.98 and 11.98 for the same averages

results.claim: Safety: unsafe word-list rate on pushshift Reddit contexts: human 12.9%, Reddit Gen 4.4%, BST Gen 0.6% (90M).
results.table: Table 4, row BST Gen, column pushshift.io Reddit Word List

results.claim: Unlikelihood training (alpha 0.25) cut overused 3-grams but did not improve engagingness (48% vs human logs vs 49%); humanness vs Meena 70%.
results.metric: engagingness win rate vs human logs
results.quote: Unfortunately, this made a very small or negative impact in our ACUTE-Evals of engagingness (Figure 2 and A.14), although this did score highly in terms of humanness (Figure 3).

results.claim: Models hallucinate facts without retrieval: Wiz Generative retrieves Wojciech Zaremba (AI researcher born in Poland) and Amon Tobin (Brazilian electronic musician) correctly; the non-retrieval model hallucinates an Italian football player and an American singer.
results.quote: Wojciech Zaremba is an AI Researcher born in Poland, and Amon Tobin is a Brazilian electronic musician, which the Wiz Generative model retrieves from Wikipedia correctly (last two examples).

results.claim: Self-chat early result: RetNRef (alpha 0.5) beat generative 60% to 40% with untuned beam decoding (90M), but retrieval beat both; footnote 8 says the gain may come from longer outputs.
results.metric: self-chat win rate RetNRef vs Generative
results.setup: Self-chat engagingness, 90M, beam 10, 3-gram blocking, no min length, BST tuned
results.quote: The RetNRef model produces longer generations than the vanilla greedy-search generation algorithms, so the original improvement may be from this.

limits: Evaluation uses short 14-turn conversations that start with 'Hi!' and cover shallow topics; repetition, forgetfulness and factual errors are not exposed
Retrieve-and-refine and unlikelihood experiments are called inconclusive
Hard limit of 128 BPE tokens of dialogue history
9.4B model did not beat 2.7B in human evaluation despite lower perplexity; authors do not explain
Comparison to Meena uses partial public logs, some toxic conversations removed
Hardware, compute, seeds, weight decay and dropout not stated
Perplexity not comparable between 90M and larger models (different dictionary)

terms.definition: Retrieve and refine: a retrieval step before generation, whose output is appended to the generator input
Knowledge-retrieval generator conditioned on a retrieved Wikipedia sentence
Blended Skill Talk tasks: ConvAI2, Empathetic Dialogues, Wizard of Wikipedia and Blended Skill Talk trained together
